paper_metadata.title: A More General Quantum Credit Risk Analysis Framework

summary: The paper proposes an enhanced quantum credit risk analysis framework based on iterative quantum amplitude estimation, tested on a 2-asset, 2-factor toy instance and on 7- to 13-qubit IBM superconducting devices. The reported experiments use 9 qubits in noiseless simulation and 7-13 qubits on hardware, but the paper emphasizes that circuit depth and decoherence prevent reliable value-at-risk/expected-loss estimation and no practical quantum advantage is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Noiseless classical simulation of the enhanced quantum credit risk analysis circuit using iterative quantum amplitude estimation for a two-asset, two-factor portfolio to estimate VaR at 95% confidence.

algorithm.variant: iterative quantum amplitude estimation (IQAE) for credit risk analysis
algorithm.convergence_criteria: target precision ϵ = 0.002 and 99% target confidence interval

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Default probabilities are encoded via Y-rotations; two qubits encode each standard normal latent factor; no sum register used in the improved LGD formulation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR_α from the CDF of total loss L by finding the smallest x_α such that P[L ≤ x_α] ≥ α, then compute Ecap = VaR_α - E[L].

problem_instance.description: Toy credit portfolio with 2 assets, real-valued LGDs, and 2 systemic risk factors.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Noiseless simulation on classical computer using Qiskit backends; latent normal variables discretized with 2 qubits each.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single noiseless simulation run reported; VaR found via bisection search using IQAE output.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Bisection search over x to locate VaR_α from estimated CDF; expected loss and VaR visualized from simulation output.

speedup_claims.conditions: for quantum amplitude estimation-based VaR estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the quadratic speedup of QAE over classical Monte Carlo, but this specific noiseless simulation does not benchmark against a classical Monte Carlo runtime or error curve.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: IQAE query complexity bounded by 1.4/ϵ · ln( (2/γ) log2(π/(4ϵ)) )
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo methods for VaR are computationally expensive; no explicit asymptotic bound given in the paper
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: Approximately 50,000 quantum samples for the reported precision/confidence setting

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 9 qubits; ~50,000 quantum samples for the reported IQAE setting (ε = 0.002, 99% confidence)
limiting_factors: No real hardware execution in this experiment
No classical runtime baseline reported for the same instance
Data loading and circuit depth overhead are discussed as major issues

notes: Hardware type inferred as simulator_other because the paper states the experiment was simulated on classical computers using Qiskit backends without a named QPU.
Circuit depth not explicitly reported for the noiseless simulation; only qubit count and sample count are stated.
The paper reports a noiseless classical simulation of the quantum circuit and does not demonstrate empirical advantage over a classical baseline.

experiments.description: Noisy simulation and real-hardware executions of the enhanced quantum credit risk analysis circuit on IBM superconducting QPUs for portfolios with 2 to 4 assets and 1 to 3 systemic risk factors.

algorithm.variant: iterative quantum amplitude estimation (IQAE) within enhanced multi-factor credit risk analysis

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Multi-factor uncertainty model with multiple rotations; each systemic risk factor has its own register in the tested configuration. The improved LGD encoding removes the sum register and uses a piecewise linear function on amplitudes.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate expected loss / VaR-related quantities for credit portfolios under the multi-factor default model.

problem_instance.description: Toy credit portfolio experiments varying from 2 to 4 assets and 1 to 3 systemic risk factors.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Data were generated by domain experts to use realistic and reliable values; public repository available.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each configuration was executed both on actual IBM hardware and via simulation of the corresponding noise model; aggregate and non-aggregate results were reported.

noise_model.mitigation_details: For each configuration, the experiment was run on the actual machine and classically via simulation of the machine’s noise model to validate the noise model and observe decoherence effects.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Reported metric was the ratio between estimated expected loss and maximum possible loss; results aggregated by configuration and architecture.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Estimates tended to converge toward half of the maximum possible loss under noise/decoherence.

results.unit: ratio of estimated expected loss to maximum possible loss

speedup_claims.conditions: IQAE used as subroutine for credit risk analysis
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper gives the IQAE query bound and an example of ~28k Grover-operator applications for a stringent precision/confidence setting, but no direct classical runtime comparison is reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: IQAE query complexity bounded by 1.4/ϵ · ln( (2/γ) log2(π/(4ϵ)) )
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo methods for VaR are computationally expensive; no explicit asymptotic bound given in the paper
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: Example given: around 28 thousand applications of the Grover operator for 99.9% confidence and 0.05% target error

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 7-13 qubits across IBM devices; noisy simulation and QPU runs on ibm_perth, ibm_lagos, ibm_canberra, ibm_algiers
limiting_factors: Circuit depth causes decoherence and loss of signal
Outputs converge toward half of the maximum possible loss rather than the target value
No quantitative classical baseline comparison showing quantum superiority
Quadratic speedup is insufficient to overcome NISQ overheads

notes: The paper reports the device names and qubit counts, but not a single fixed qubit count for all configurations; the range 7–13 is reported across experiments.
Circuit depth is discussed qualitatively as large and causing decoherence, but no numeric depth is given.
The paper explicitly states that the depth of the circuit prevents correct extrapolation of the expected value and that results are mainly a baseline for future work, not a demonstrated advantage.
